draft.title: Dark mode / theming decision (web)
draft.principle_summary: Two converging bodies of evidence back a light-only web canon: (1) the positive-polarity-advantage literature shows dark-text-on-light beats light-on-dark for reading/proofreading/visual-acuity tasks across ages, with the advantage growing as type shrinks, so light-only is not a readability compromise; (2) Nielsen Norman Group's applied guidance is that a HALF-supported dark mode is worse than none, if you ship it you must ship both themes fully and maintain contrast (WCAG-then-APCA) separately for each, which is a real, ongoing QA and design-token tax. Solen's actual constraint is that the owner explicitly declined web dark mode (cost/priority call, TASTE_LOG 2026-07-15, graveyarded in REMOVED.md), not that dark mode is objectively bad; the perceptual research explains why declining it costs nothing on the readability axis, and the maintenance-cost argument explains why it would cost something on the engineering axis. Mobile keeps the only dark surface (Revolut-charcoal, owner preference, canonized in solen-mobile THEMING.md) precisely because that surface was fully built and tested, honoring NN/g's "commit to both or don't ship it" rule.

sources.claim: Dark-text-on-light-background (positive polarity) outperforms light-on-dark (negative polarity) on visual-acuity and proofreading tasks, for both younger and older adults; the advantage grows as character size shrinks. Mechanism: higher luminance of a light background constricts the pupil, producing a sharper retinal image.
sources.source: Piepenbrock, Mayr, Mund & Buchner (2013), 'Positive display polarity is advantageous for both younger and older adults', Ergonomics; Piepenbrock, Mayr & Buchner (2014), 'Positive Display Polarity Is Particularly Advantageous for Small Character Sizes', Human Factors Vol 56, SAGE doi 10.1177/0018720813515509

sources.claim: If a product supports dark mode, it should fully support BOTH light and dark themes rather than a half-built dark mode; dark mode's real benefits are reduced glare/eye strain in low light and OLED battery savings, not objective readability, since NN/g's own review of the polarity literature found light mode wins readability and proofreading tasks across dimensions.
sources.source: Nielsen Norman Group, 'Dark Mode vs. Light Mode: Which Is Better?', nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode

sources.claim: WCAG 2's contrast formula overstates contrast for dark colour pairs (a numerically passing ratio near black can still be functionally unreadable), so a dark theme needs the APCA supplement to actually verify, which a light-only surface does not need.
sources.source: Already documented in Solen's own RATIONALE.md lines 99-101 (APCA/WCAG known-weakness note); consistent with the published limitations of the WCAG 2 formula that motivated the WCAG 3 APCA candidate

sources.claim: Roughly 82% of mobile users use dark mode and 70% report readability issues from poor contrast.
sources.source: Unsourced marketing/listicle figures surfaced in secondary search results (dark-mode trend blog posts); no primary study located backing either number

draft.solen_current: The decision itself is already made and recorded, but scattered, not consolidated into one theming domain section as the stream's target_anchor asks for. Evidence already in the repo: RATIONALE.md line 5 (v2 changelog: "dark-mode polarity recorded as a mobile-canon pointer only, web dark mode stays graveyarded"); lines 99-101 (WCAG 2 known-weakness on dark pairs, APCA supplement policy); line 667 (owner verbatim "no dark mode", 2026-07-15 probe pick); line 723, Domain 14 "depth, light, and materiality" (positive polarity advantage T1, Buchner/Piepenbrock, explicitly stated as BOUNDARY: "on web this only confirms the default...It BINDS the mobile dark canon...Pointer only; the mobile file is the canon"). REMOVED.md line 72 records the graveyard entry with the TASTE_LOG citation. solen-mobile/_design-system/THEMING.md is the actual canon file (380 lines, canonized 2026-07-12), covering the light=Uber-style / dark=Revolut-charcoal split, ThemeProvider architecture, and why dual-theme exists on mobile only (owner's personal dark-mode habit, verified via Mobbin that Uber itself is light-only).
draft.gap: The polarity research (T1) already lives in RATIONALE.md's Domain 14 as one sentence with a BOUNDARY clause pointing at web, but there is no standalone "theming contract" block that states the DECISION explicitly, names its FORCES, and gives readers (including future subagents grepping for "dark mode") one place to land instead of reconstructing the story from four scattered line references plus a REMOVED.md entry plus a cross-repo file. A subagent or new contributor searching RATIONALE.md top-to-bottom for "why no web dark mode" currently has to piece together lines 5, 99-101, 667, and 723 to get the full picture; there is also no NN/g-sourced maintenance-cost argument anywhere in the file, only the perceptual argument, so the doc currently reads as "dark mode is worse to read" rather than the more honest "dark mode costs QA/build effort AND doesn't buy readability, and the owner chose not to pay that cost on web."
draft.proposed_addition:
Insert as a new numbered domain section in RATIONALE.md (after section 19 "Domain 15: color-token architecture" or as a new final section near 28, either placement works since it is a pointer, not a token definition):

## Domain: Theming Contract (web light-only, mobile dual-theme)

DECISION: web ships light-only by design. Mobile is the sole owner of dark mode (solen-mobile/_design-system/THEMING.md is canon, canonized 2026-07-12). This is not an omission; it is a recorded, dated owner decision (TASTE_LOG.md 2026-07-15, owner verbatim "no dark mode"; graveyarded in REMOVED.md line 72).

FORCES:
1. Perceptual: positive-polarity advantage (T1, Piepenbrock/Buchner) shows dark-on-light beats light-on-dark on reading and visual-acuity tasks for all ages, advantage growing as type shrinks. Declining web dark mode costs nothing on the readability axis, it is the empirically favored default already.
2. Engineering/QA cost: NN/g (T2) frames dark mode as an all-or-nothing commitment, a half-built dark theme is worse than none. Full support means duplicating every token pass through both a light AND dark palette, and re-verifying contrast with the APCA supplement (T1, RATIONALE.md lines 99-101) because WCAG 2's formula is known-weak specifically on dark pairs. That is a second contrast-QA surface Solen does not currently need to open.
3. Product priority: mobile already fully built and shipped its dark canon (Revolut-charcoal, owner's personal habit, THEMING.md section 0) satisfying NN/g's "commit to both" rule on the one surface where the owner actually uses it daily. Web has no comparable forcing function.

OPTIMIZES FOR: shipping velocity and QA surface area on web (one palette, one contrast pass, no theme-switch state machine); honoring an explicit, dated owner call rather than re-litigating it.

SACRIFICES: web users who personally prefer dark mode get no accommodation (a real, acknowledged tradeoff, not a myth-based one); the site cannot claim "supports your system theme" as a feature.

BOUNDARY: this is a maintenance-cost and owner-preference argument, not a "dark mode is bad" claim. NN/g's own recommendation, if a team DOES build dark mode, is to build it fully and let the user choose. Nothing here overrides that guidance for mobile; it only explains why web opted out. If the owner ever reverses the 2026-07-15 call, this section's FORCES 1 and 2 still apply as design constraints on execution (full parity, not a half theme; APCA-verify every pair), FORCE 3 (no forcing function) would simply become moot.

MECHANIC: positive-polarity T1 study details as listed in numbers_used; NN/g "all-or-nothing" recommendation T2; WCAG 2 dark-pair weakness T1 (already documented, cross-referenced not restated).

SOURCE: Piepenbrock et al. 2013 (Ergonomics), Piepenbrock, Mayr & Buchner 2014 (Human Factors, SAGE doi 10.1177/0018720813515509); Nielsen Norman Group, nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode; RATIONALE.md internal cross-refs lines 99-101, 667, 723; REMOVED.md line 72; solen-mobile/_design-system/THEMING.md section 0.

XREF: mobile theming canon lives entirely in solen-mobile/_design-system/THEMING.md, do not duplicate its ThemeProvider/palette mechanics here, this section only explains the WEB decision and its evidentiary grounding.

## Domain: Theming Contract (web light-only, mobile dual-theme)

DECISION: web ships light-only by design. Mobile is the sole owner of dark mode (solen-mobile/_design-system/THEMING.md is canon, canonized 2026-07-12). This is not an omission, it is a recorded, dated owner decision (TASTE_LOG.md 2026-07-15, owner verbatim "no dark mode", graveyarded in REMOVED.md line 72).

FORCES:
1. Perceptual (T1): the positive-polarity advantage (Piepenbrock, Mayr, Mund and Buchner 2013, "Positive display polarity is advantageous for both younger and older adults"; Piepenbrock, Mayr and Buchner 2014, "Positive Display Polarity Is Particularly Advantageous for Small Character Sizes", Human Factors, doi 10.1177/0018720813515509) shows dark-on-light beats light-on-dark on reading and visual-acuity tasks for all ages, and the advantage grows as type shrinks (mechanism: the brighter background constricts the pupil, sharpening the retinal image). Declining web dark mode costs nothing on the readability axis, it is the empirically favored default already.
2. Engineering and QA cost (T2): Nielsen Norman Group's applied guidance (nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode) is that dark mode is an all-or-nothing commitment: their own review of the polarity literature found light mode wins on visual performance for normal vision, dark mode's real benefit is reduced eye fatigue in dim environments (a small effect), and shipping it well takes real design and QA time because most designs are built light-first. Full support means duplicating every token pass through both a light and dark palette, and re-verifying contrast with the APCA supplement (T1, RATIONALE.md lines 99-101) because WCAG 2's formula is known-weak specifically on dark pairs. That is a second contrast-QA surface Solen does not currently need to open.
3. Product priority: mobile already fully built and shipped its dark canon (Revolut-charcoal, owner's personal habit, THEMING.md section 0), satisfying NN/g's "commit to it properly" guidance on the one surface where the owner actually uses it daily. Web has no comparable forcing function.

OPTIMIZES FOR: shipping velocity and QA surface area on web (one palette, one contrast pass, no theme-switch state machine), honoring an explicit, dated owner call rather than re-litigating it.

SACRIFICES: web users who personally prefer dark mode get no accommodation (a real, acknowledged tradeoff, not a myth-based one). The site cannot claim "supports your system theme" as a feature.

BOUNDARY: this is a maintenance-cost and owner-preference argument, not a "dark mode is bad" claim. NN/g's own recommendation, if a team does build dark mode, is to build it properly and test it, not to skip it out of readability fear. Nothing here overrides that guidance for mobile, it only explains why web opted out. If the owner ever reverses the 2026-07-15 call, this section's FORCES 1 and 2 still apply as design constraints on execution (full parity, not a half theme, APCA-verify every pair); FORCE 3 (no forcing function) would simply become moot.

MECHANIC: positive-polarity T1 findings as above; NN/g's "commit fully or don't bother" applied guidance, T2; WCAG 2 dark-pair weakness, T1, already documented, cross-referenced not restated.

SOURCE: Piepenbrock, Mayr, Mund and Buchner 2013 (PubMed 23654206); Piepenbrock, Mayr and Buchner 2014 (Human Factors, SAGE doi 10.1177/0018720813515509); Nielsen Norman Group, nngroup.com/articles/dark-mode; RATIONALE.md internal cross-refs lines 5, 99-101, section 15 (owner verbatim pick), section 18 Domain 14; REMOVED.md line 72; TASTE_LOG.md 2026-07-15 entry; solen-mobile/_design-system/THEMING.md section 0.
